skill_drafts.name: Custom Observation Convention Registration
skill_drafts.description: Register custom Micrometer observation conventions as Spring beans to replace default observation behavior in Spring Boot 3.0 applications. This micro-skill enables extension of high-cardinality and low-cardinality key values for server request observations.
applicable_signals: need to customize high-cardinality key values for observations
need to customize low-cardinality key values for observations
contraindications: Using only default observation behavior without customization
Applying post-processing filters instead of convention replacement
Attempting to modify observations after they are created
intervention_moves: Create a custom class implementing the observation convention interface
Reuse standard key names from ObservationDocumentation
Wrap the custom convention in a @Configuration class with @Bean method
Deploy the bean to the application context
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create custom observation convention class', 'detail': 'Implement the appropriate convention interface (e.g., ServerRequestObservationConvention) with getHighCardinalityKeyValues() and getLowCardinalityKeyValues() methods'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Reuse standard key names', 'detail': 'Reference ObservationDocumentation constants for key names to maintain consistency'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Create @Configuration class', 'detail': 'Define a configuration class annotated with @Configuration'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Register bean', 'detail': 'Add @Bean method that instantiates and returns the custom convention'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify registration', 'detail': 'Confirm the bean is picked up by auto-configuration and replaces the default convention'}
triggers: need to customize high-cardinality or low-cardinality key values for server request observations; replacing default Micrometer conventions
constraints: Custom convention must be registered as a Spring bean
Bean must be discoverable by Spring Boot auto-configuration
Convention should reuse standard key names from ObservationDocumentation where applicable
cautions: Do not use ObservationFilter if you need to replace the entire convention; filters are post-processing only
Ensure custom convention does not conflict with other registered conventions
output_contract: Custom observation convention bean is registered in the application context and automatically picked up by Spring Boot auto-configuration, replacing the default observation convention for all matching observation contexts.

examples.input: Need to add custom HTTP URL key values to server request observations
examples.output: ExtendedServerRequestObservationConvention bean registered; getHighCardinalityKeyValues() returns custom KeyValues.of(httpUrl(context))
examples.notes: Convention is applied automatically to all ServerRequestObservationContext instances

examples.input: Need to customize low-cardinality method key values
examples.notes: Reuses standard key name from ObservationDocumentation

metadata.prompt: Create a @Configuration class with a @Bean method that returns your custom observation convention implementation (e.g., ExtendedServerRequestObservationConvention). The bean will be automatically picked up by Spring Boot's auto-configuration and replace the default convention. Ensure your custom convention implements the appropriate ObservationDocumentation interface and reuses standard key names where possible.

skill_drafts.name: Observation Filter Post-Processing
skill_drafts.description: Apply custom ObservationFilter beans to add or remove key values from observations without replacing the default convention. Filters act as composable post-processing components that augment or modify observation metadata after the default convention has been applied.
applicable_signals: observation convention is already in place and working
additional key-value filtering or enrichment is required
contraindications: need to replace the entire observation convention (use ObservationConvention instead)
filters are additive only and cannot remove all default behavior
workflow_steps: Create a class implementing ObservationFilter interface
Implement filter logic to add or remove KeyValue entries from observations
Register the filter as a @Bean in a @Configuration class
Verify the filter is picked up by auto-configuration and applied to observations
triggers: need to augment observation key values without replacing the entire convention
post-processing observations to add or remove metadata
constraints: filter bean must be registered in the application context for auto-discovery
filters are applied after the default convention
cautions: filters do not replace the default convention; they are post-processors only
multiple filters can be composed; ensure they do not conflict
output_contract: ObservationFilter bean is registered and applied as a post-processing component; observation key values are modified according to filter logic; default convention remains active.

metadata.prompt: Implement an ObservationFilter bean to add or remove key values from observations. Register the filter as a bean in the application context; it will be picked up by auto-configuration and applied as a post-processing step. Filters do not replace the default observation convention—they are additive and composable.

skill_drafts.name: Spring Data Property Prefix Migration
skill_drafts.description: Migrate application configuration properties from legacy spring.data.* prefixes to module-specific prefixes (e.g., spring.cassandra.*, spring.redis.*) when upgrading to Spring Boot 3.0. The spring.data prefix is now reserved for Spring Data framework use, and properties under it imply Spring Data is required on the classpath.
applicable_signals: Build or startup logs show unrecognized spring.data.* properties
Spring Data module is on classpath but configuration is not being picked up
Migration checklist or upgrade guide references data property changes
contraindications: Application does not use Spring Data modules or data access layer
No spring.data.* properties present in configuration
Application is not upgrading to Spring Boot 3.0
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify all spring.data.* properties in application.properties or application.yml'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Map each property to its module-specific prefix (e.g., spring.data.cassandra.* → spring.cassandra.*)'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Rebuild and start application; verify no configuration errors in logs'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Test data connectivity for each affected module (Cassandra, Redis, etc.)'}
triggers: Upgrading Spring Boot application from 2.x to 3.0
Application uses Spring Data modules (Cassandra, Redis, MongoDB, etc.)
Configuration files contain spring.data.* property prefixes
constraints: All spring.data.* properties must be identified before migration begins
Module-specific prefix mappings must be verified against Spring Data release notes
Application context must successfully load after property migration
cautions: Incomplete migration may cause silent configuration failures; validate all data modules after relocation
Some properties may have been renamed or removed in Spring Data; consult release notes for each module
output_contract: All spring.data.* properties successfully remapped to module-specific prefixes; application configuration loads without errors; data module connectivity verified.

metadata.prompt: Review all application.properties or application.yml files for properties using spring.data.* prefixes. For each data module (Cassandra, Redis, MongoDB, etc.), relocate properties to their module-specific prefix. Validate that the application context loads without configuration errors and that data connectivity is restored.
